nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a real-rooted complex polynomial of positive degree, and let $\rho(p)$ be the largest real part of a root of $p$. Then the real number $\rho(p)$, viewed as a complex number, is a root of $p$.
nodes.title: For a real-rooted polynomial, the largest real part of a root is a root

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a monic real-rooted complex polynomial, and let $\rho(p)$ be the largest real part of a root of $p$, or $0$ if $p$ has no roots. Then $\operatorname{Re} p(x) \ge 0$ for every real number $x \ge \rho(p)$.
nodes.title: Monic real-rooted polynomials have nonnegative real part from the largest root on

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a monic real-rooted complex polynomial, and let $\rho(p)$ be the largest real part of a root of $p$, or $0$ if $p$ has no roots. Then $\operatorname{Re} p(x) > 0$ for every real number $x > \rho(p)$.
nodes.title: Monic real-rooted polynomials have positive real part right of the largest root

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a complex polynomial whose multiset of roots is nonempty, and let $\rho(p)$ be the largest real part of a root of $p$. Then some root $z$ of $p$ satisfies $\operatorname{Re} z = \rho(p)$.
nodes.title: The largest real part of a root is attained

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a nonzero complex polynomial that is unchanged when complex conjugation is applied to each of its coefficients. If every root $z$ of $p$ satisfies $\operatorname{Im} z \le 0$, then $p$ is real-rooted.
nodes.title: Conjugation-invariant polynomials with roots in the closed lower half-plane are real-rooted

nodes.summary: A complex polynomial $p$ is real-rooted if every element $z$ of its multiset of roots is real, that is, $\operatorname{Im} z = 0$.
nodes.title: Real-rooted polynomials

nodes.summary: For a complex polynomial $p$, let $\rho(p)$ be the largest real part $\operatorname{Re} z$ of an element $z$ of the multiset of roots of $p$, with $\rho(p) = 0$ when that multiset is empty (as it is for nonzero constants and for $p = 0$).
nodes.title: Largest real part of a root

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a complex polynomial and let $\rho(p)$ be the largest real part of an element of its multiset of roots, or $0$ if that multiset is empty. Then every element $z$ of the multiset of roots of $p$ satisfies $\operatorname{Re} z \le \rho(p)$.
nodes.title: Real parts of roots are bounded by the largest one

nodes.summary: Every complex polynomial of positive degree has at least one root.
nodes.title: Nonconstant complex polynomials have a root

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
